passages.question: Who made the world?
passages.answer: God made the world.

passages.question: Who is God?
passages.answer: God is the Creator of heaven and earth, and of all things.

passages.question: What is man?
passages.answer: Man is a creature composed of body and soul, and made to the image and likeness of God.

passages.question: Is this likeness in the body or in the soul?
passages.answer: This likeness is chiefly in the soul.

passages.question: How is the soul like to God?
passages.answer: The soul is like God because it is a spirit that will never die, and has understanding and free will.

passages.question: Why did God make you?
passages.answer: God made me to know Him, to love Him, and to serve Him in this world, and to be happy with Him forever in the next.

passages.question: Of which must we take more care, our soul or our body?
passages.answer: We must take more care of our soul than of our body.

passages.question: Why must we take more care of our soul than of our body?
passages.answer: We must take more care of our soul than of our body, because in losing our soul we lose God and everlasting happiness.

passages.question: What must we do to save our souls?
passages.answer: To save our souls we must worship God by faith, hope, and charity; that is, we must believe in Him, hope in Him, and love Him with all our heart.

passages.question: How shall we know the things which we are to believe?
passages.answer: We shall know the things which we are to believe from the Catholic Church, through which God speaks to us.

passages.question: Where shall we find the chief truths which the Church teaches?
passages.answer: We shall find the chief truths which the Church teaches in the Apostles' Creed.

passages.question: What is a Sacrament?
passages.answer: A Sacrament is an outward sign instituted by Christ to give grace.

passages.question: How many Sacraments are there?
passages.answer: There are seven Sacraments: Baptism, Confirmation, Holy Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Holy Orders, and Matrimony.

passages.question: Whence have the Sacraments the power of giving grace?
passages.answer: The Sacraments have the power of giving grace from the merits of Jesus Christ.

passages.question: What grace do the Sacraments give?
passages.answer: Some of the Sacraments give sanctifying grace, and others increase it in our souls.

passages.question: Which are the Sacraments that give sanctifying grace?
passages.answer: The Sacraments that give sanctifying grace are Baptism and Penance; and they are called Sacraments of the dead.

passages.question: Why are Baptism and Penance called Sacraments of the dead?
passages.answer: Baptism and Penance are called Sacraments of the dead, because they take away sin, which is the death of the soul, and give grace, which is its life.

passages.question: What is Baptism?
passages.answer: Baptism is a Sacrament which cleanses us from original sin, makes us Christians, children of God, and heirs of heaven.

passages.question: Are actual sins ever remitted by Baptism?
passages.answer: Actual sins and all the punishment due to them are remitted by Baptism, if the person baptized be guilty of any.

passages.question: Is Baptism necessary to salvation?
passages.answer: Baptism is necessary to salvation, because without it we cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven.

passages.question: Who can administer Baptism?
passages.answer: The priest is the ordinary minister of Baptism; but in case of necessity any one who has the use of reason may baptize.

passages.question: How is Baptism given?
passages.answer: Whoever baptizes should pour water on the head of the person to be baptized, and say, while pouring the water: I baptize thee in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

passages.question: How many kinds of Baptism are there?
passages.answer: There are three kinds of Baptism: Baptism of water, of desire, and of blood.

passages.question: What is Confirmation?
passages.answer: Confirmation is a Sacrament through which we receive the Holy Ghost to make us strong and perfect Christians and soldiers of Jesus Christ.

passages.question: Who administers Confirmation?
passages.answer: The bishop is the ordinary minister of Confirmation.

passages.question: How does the bishop give Confirmation?
passages.answer: The bishop extends his hands over those who are to be confirmed, prays that they may receive the Holy Ghost, and anoints the forehead of each with holy chrism in the form of a cross.

passages.question: What is holy chrism?
passages.answer: Holy chrism is a mixture of olive-oil and balm, consecrated by the bishop.

passages.question: What does the bishop say in anointing the person he confirms?
passages.answer: In anointing the person he confirms the bishop says: I sign thee with the sign of the cross, and I confirm thee with the chrism of salvation, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

passages.question: What is meant by anointing the forehead with chrism in the form of a cross?
passages.answer: By anointing the forehead with chrism in the form of a cross is meant, that the Christian who is confirmed must openly profess and practice his faith, never be ashamed of it, and rather die than deny it.

passages.question: Why does the bishop give the person he confirms a slight blow on the cheek?
passages.answer: The bishop gives the person he confirms a slight blow on the cheek, to put him in mind that he must be ready to suffer everything, even death, for the sake of Christ.

passages.question: To receive Confirmation worthily is it necessary to be in the state of grace?
passages.answer: To receive Confirmation worthily it is necessary to be in the state of grace.

passages.question: What special preparation should be made to receive Confirmation?
passages.answer: Persons of an age to learn should know the chief mysteries of faith and the duties of a Christian, and be instructed in the nature and effects of this Sacrament.

passages.question: Is it a sin to neglect Confirmation?
passages.answer: It is a sin to neglect Confirmation, especially in these evil days when faith and morals are exposed to so many and such violent temptations.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Which are the effects of Confirmation?
passages.answer: The effects of Confirmation are an increase of sanctifying grace, the strengthening of our faith, and the gifts of the Holy Ghost.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Which are the gifts of the Holy Ghost?
passages.answer: The gifts of the Holy Ghost are Wisdom, Understanding, Counsel, Fortitude, Knowledge, Piety and Fear of the Lord.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Why do we receive the gift of Fear of the Lord?
passages.answer: We receive the gift of Fear of the Lord to fill us with a dread of sin.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Why do we receive the gift of Piety?
passages.answer: We receive the gift of Piety to make us love God as a Father and obey Him because we love Him.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Why do we receive the gift of Knowledge?
passages.answer: We receive the gift of Knowledge to enable us to discover the will of God in all things.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Why do we receive the gift of Fortitude?
passages.answer: We receive the gift of Fortitude to strengthen us to do the will of God in all things.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Why do we receive the gift of Counsel?
passages.answer: We receive the gift of Counsel to warn us of the deceits of the devil, and of the dangers to salvation.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Why do we receive the gift of Understanding?
passages.answer: We receive the gift of Understanding to enable us to know more clearly the mysteries of faith.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Why do we receive the gift of Wisdom?
passages.answer: We receive the gift of Wisdom to give us a relish for the things of God, and to direct our whole life and all our actions to His honor and glory.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Which are the Beatitudes?
passages.answer: The Beatitudes are: 1. Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. 2. Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land. 3. Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted. 4. Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice, for they shall be filled. 5. Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. 6. Blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see God. 7. Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God. 8. Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

passages.lesson: On the Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Ghost
passages.question: Which are the twelve fruits of the Holy Ghost?
passages.answer: The twelve fruits of the Holy Ghost are Charity, Joy, Peace, Patience, Benignity, Goodness, Long-suffering, Mildness, Faith, Modesty, Continency, and Chastity.

passages.question: What is the Sacrament of Penance?
passages.answer: Penance is a Sacrament in which the sins committed after Baptism are forgiven.

passages.question: How does the Sacrament of Penance remit sin, and restore to the soul the friendship of God?
passages.answer: The Sacrament of Penance remits sins and restores the friendship of God to the soul by means of the absolution of the priest.

passages.question: How do you know that the priest has the power of absolving from the sins committed after Baptism?
passages.answer: I know that the priest has the power of absolving from the sins committed after Baptism, because Jesus Christ granted that power to the priests of His Church when He said: "Receive ye the Holy Ghost. Whose sins you shall forgive, they are forgiven them; whose sins you shall retain, they are retained."

passages.question: How do the priests of the Church exercise the power of forgiving sins?
passages.answer: The priests of the Church exercise the power of forgiving sins by hearing the confession of sins, and granting pardon for them as ministers of God and in His name.

passages.question: What must we do to receive the Sacrament of Penance worthily?
passages.answer: To receive the Sacrament of Penance worthily we must do five things: 1. We must examine our conscience. 2. We must have sorrow for our sins. 3. We must make a firm resolution never more to offend God. 4. We must confess our sins to the priest. 5. We must accept the penance which the priest gives us.

passages.question: What is the examination of conscience?
passages.answer: The examination of conscience is an earnest effort to recall to mind all the sins we have committed since our last worthy confession.

passages.question: How can we make a good examination of conscience?
passages.answer: We can make a good examination of conscience by calling to memory the commandments of God, the precepts of the Church, the seven capital sins, and the particular duties of our state in life, to find out the sins we have committed.

passages.question: What should we do before beginning the examination of conscience?
passages.answer: Before beginning the examination of conscience we should pray to God to give us light to know our sins and grace to detest them.

passages.question: What is contrition, or sorrow for sin?
passages.answer: Contrition, or sorrow for sin, is a hatred of sin and a true grief of the soul for having offended God, with a firm purpose of sinning no more.

passages.question: What kind of sorrow should we have for our sins?
passages.answer: The sorrow we should have for our sins should be interior, supernatural, universal, and sovereign.

passages.question: What do you mean by saying that our sorrow should be interior?
passages.answer: When I say that our sorrow should be interior, I mean that it should come from the heart, and not merely from the lips.

passages.question: What do you mean by saying that our sorrow should be supernatural?
passages.answer: When I say that our sorrow should be supernatural, I mean that it should be prompted by the grace of God, and excited by motives which spring from faith, and not by merely natural motives.

passages.question: What do you mean by saying that our sorrow should be universal?
passages.answer: When I say that our sorrow should be universal, I mean that we should be sorry for all our mortal sins without exception.

passages.question: What do you mean when you say that our sorrow should be sovereign?
passages.answer: When I say that our sorrow should be sovereign, I mean that we should grieve more for having offended God than for any other evil that can befall us.

passages.question: Why should we be sorry for our sins?
passages.answer: We should be sorry for our sins, because sin is the greatest of evils and an offense against God our Creator, Preserver, and Redeemer, and because it shuts us out of heaven and condemns us to the eternal pains of hell.

passages.question: How many kinds of contrition are there?
passages.answer: There are two kinds of contrition: perfect contrition and imperfect contrition.

passages.question: What is perfect contrition?
passages.answer: Perfect contrition is that which fills us with sorrow and hatred for sin, because it offends God, who is infinitely good in Himself and worthy of all love.

passages.question: What is imperfect contrition?
passages.answer: Imperfect contrition is that by which we hate what offends God, because by it we lose heaven and deserve hell; or because sin is so hateful in itself.

passages.question: Is imperfect contrition sufficient for a worthy confession?
passages.answer: Imperfect contrition is sufficient for a worthy confession, but we should endeavor to have perfect contrition.

passages.question: What do you mean by a firm purpose of sinning no more?
passages.answer: By a firm purpose of sinning no more I mean a fixed resolve not only to avoid all mortal sin, but also its near occasions.

passages.question: What do you mean by the near occasions of sin?
passages.answer: By the near occasions of sin I mean all the persons, places, and things that may easily lead us into sin.

passages.question: What is Confession?
passages.answer: Confession is the telling of our sins to a duly authorized priest, for the purpose of obtaining forgiveness.

passages.question: What sins are we bound to confess?
passages.answer: We are bound to confess all our mortal sins, but it is well also to confess our venial sins.

passages.question: Which are the chief qualities of a good Confession?
passages.answer: The chief qualities of a good Confession are three: it must be humble, sincere, and entire.

passages.question: When is our Confession humble?
passages.answer: Our Confession is humble, when we accuse our selves of our sins, with a deep sense of shame and sorrow for having offended God.

passages.question: When is our Confession sincere?
passages.answer: Our Confession is sincere, when we tell our sins honestly and truthfully, neither exaggerating nor excusing them.

passages.question: When is our Confession entire?
passages.answer: Our Confession is entire, when we tell the number and kinds of our sins and the circumstances which change their nature.

passages.question: What should we do if we cannot remember the number of our sins?
passages.answer: If we cannot remember the number of our sins, we should tell the number as nearly as possible, and say how often we may have sinned in a day, a week, or a month, and how long the habit or practice has lasted.

passages.question: Is our Confession worthy if, without our fault, we forget to confess a mortal sin?
passages.answer: If without our fault we forget to confess a mortal sin, our Confession is worthy, and the sin is forgiven; but it must be told in Confession if it again comes to our mind.

passages.question: Is it a grievous offense wilfully to conceal a mortal sin in Confession?
passages.answer: It is a grievous offense wilfully to conceal a mortal sin in Confession, because we thereby tell a lie to the Holy Ghost, and make our Confession worthless.

passages.question: What must he do who has wilfully concealed a mortal sin in Confession?
passages.answer: He who has wilfully concealed a mortal sin in Confession must not only confess it, but must also repeat all the sins he has committed since his last worthy Confession.

passages.question: Why does the priest give us a penance after Confession?
passages.answer: The priest gives us a penance after Confession, that we may satisfy God for the temporal punishment due to our sins.

passages.question: Does not the Sacrament of Penance remit all punishment due to sin?
passages.answer: The Sacrament of Penance remits the eternal punishment due to sin, but it does not always remit the temporal punishment which God requires as satisfaction for our sins.

passages.question: Why does God require a temporal punishment as a satisfaction for sin?
passages.answer: God requires a temporal punishment as a satisfaction for sin, to teach us the great evil of sin and to prevent us from falling again.

passages.question: Which are the chief means by which we satisfy God for the temporal punishment due to sin?
passages.answer: The chief means by which we satisfy God for the temporal punishment due to sin are: Prayer, Fasting, Almsgiving, all spiritual and corporal works of mercy, and the patient suffering of the ills of life.

passages.question: Which are the chief spiritual works of mercy?
passages.answer: The chief spiritual works of mercy are seven: To admonish the sinner, to instruct the ignorant, to counsel the doubtful, to comfort the sorrowful, to bear wrongs patiently, to forgive all injuries, and to pray for the living and the dead.

passages.question: Which are the chief corporal works of mercy?
passages.answer: The chief corporal works of mercy are seven: To feed the hungry, to give drink to the thirsty, to clothe the naked, to ransom the captive, to harbor the harborless, to visit the sick, and to bury the dead.

passages.question: What is the Holy Eucharist?
passages.answer: The Holy Eucharist is the Sacrament which contains the body and blood, soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ under the appearances of bread and wine.

passages.question: When did Christ institute the Holy Eucharist?
passages.answer: Christ instituted the Holy Eucharist at the Last Supper, the night before He died.

passages.question: Who were present when our Lord instituted the Holy Eucharist?
passages.answer: When our Lord instituted the Holy Eucharist the twelve Apostles were present.

passages.question: Is Jesus Christ whole and entire both under the form of bread and under the form of wine?
passages.answer: Jesus Christ is whole and entire both under the form of bread and under the form of wine.

passages.question: Did anything remain of the bread and wine after their substance had been changed into the substance of the body and blood of our Lord?
passages.answer: After the substance of the bread and wine had been changed into the substance of the body and blood of our Lord there remained only the appearances of bread and wine.

passages.question: What do you mean by the appearances of bread and wine?
passages.answer: By the appearances of bread and wine I mean the figure, the color, the taste, and whatever appears to the senses.

passages.question: What is this change of the bread and wine into the body and blood of our Lord called?
passages.answer: This change of the bread and wine into the body and blood of our Lord is called Transubstantiation.

passages.question: How was the substance of the bread and wine changed into the substance of the body and blood of Christ?
passages.answer: The substance of the bread and wine was changed into the substance of the body and blood of Christ by His almighty power.

passages.question: Does this change of bread and wine into the body and blood of Christ continue to be made in the Church?
passages.answer: This change of bread and wine into the body and blood of Christ continues to be made in the Church by Jesus Christ through the ministry of His priests.

passages.question: Is there any other means of obtaining God's grace than the Sacraments?
passages.answer: There is another means of obtaining God's grace, and it is prayer.

passages.question: What is prayer?
passages.answer: Prayer is the lifting up of our minds and hearts to God to adore Him, to thank Him for His benefits, to ask His forgiveness, and to beg of Him all the graces we need whether for soul or body.

passages.question: Is prayer necessary to salvation?
passages.answer: Prayer is necessary to salvation, and without it no one having the use of reason can be saved.

passages.question: At what particular times should we pray?
passages.answer: We should pray particularly on Sundays and holydays, every morning and night, in all dangers, temptations, and afflictions.

passages.question: How should we pray?
passages.answer: We should pray: 1st, With attention; 2d, With a sense of our own helplessness and dependence upon God; 3d, With a great desire for the graces we beg of God; 4th, With trust in God's goodness; 5th, With perseverance.
